struck: Every owner named in the contract is an "owner" for this law, so co-owners each have the duty and each signs.
use: The law's duty falls on each owner named in the contract. The form has signature lines for the owners.

struck: No exemption covers an investor, a landlord, a second-home owner or a company that owns the home.
use: The law lists no exemption for an investor, a landlord, a second-home owner or a company. A rental you never lived in still needs the form, unless the sale is one of the 15 exempt kinds.
The form has nine parts of questions, one for each subject the law names, and a last part for explaining your Yes answers.

struck: About 1 in 3 homes in Horry County (37 percent) has a last recorded sale from before Hurricane Florence in September 2018.
use: More than 1 in 3 homes in Horry County (37 percent) last sold before Hurricane Florence in September 2018.

struck: For those owners, the form's questions about "your ownership" reach back over those storms.
use: If you have owned your home since before those storms, the form's questions about "your ownership" cover them.

pattern: \bseaward of the state's setback line, so their (?:sale )?contracts need
struck: About 10,700 residential parcels with a building in Horry County lie at least partly seaward of the state's setback line, so their sale contracts need the beachfront disclosure.
use: By our count from the state's and the county's maps, about 10,700 homes in Horry County sit on lots that reach seaward of the state's setback line. A survey settles where the line falls on a given lot.

struck: from 1 percent in Carolina Forest to about 1 in 3 in Conway
use: more than half in Loris, about 1 in 3 in Conway and Surfside Beach, 28 percent in Myrtle Beach, 19 percent in North Myrtle Beach, and about 1 percent in Carolina Forest

pattern: \b(?:bookings|rentals?) that begin within 90 days after the deed is recorded
struck: A buyer takes the home subject to vacation rental bookings that begin within 90 days after the deed is recorded.
use: Under the state's Vacation Rental Act, the buyer takes the home subject to rentals that begin within 90 days after the deed is recorded. That act does not cover a condo rented through a hotel-style front desk.

struck: South Carolina gives three years to bring many kinds of claims, including claims on a contract and for fraud; for fraud the time starts when the buyer discovers it.
use: Many claims in South Carolina must be filed within three years. When the clock starts depends on the claim; an attorney can say which applies.

pattern: \bsignificantly lowers the value or the soundness of the home
struck: a fact that significantly lowers the value or the soundness of the home
use: a problem that significantly lowers the home's value or soundness, or is a significant health risk to the people who live there
